name: Worry and Unbelief

counsel.text: We are bid to "commit our way unto the Lord;" (Ps. 37. 5) the Hebrew word is, "roll thy way upon the Lord." It is our work to cast away care; (1 Pe 5. 7) and it is God's work to take care.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 1

counsel.text: By our immoderacy we take his work out of his hand. Care, when it is eccentric, either distrustful or distracting, is very dishonourable to God; it takes away his providence, as if he sat in heaven and minded not what became of things here below; like a man that makes a clock, and then leaves it to go for itself.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 1

counsel.text: God takes care of every saint in particular, as if he had none else to care for.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the providence of God

counsel.text: Let it be an antidote against immoderate fear, that nothing comes to pass but what is ordained by God's decree, and ordered by his providence. We sometimes fear what the issue of things will be, when men grow high in their actings; but let us not make things worse by our fear. Men are limited in their power, and cannot go one hair's breadth further than God's providence permits.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, the providence of God

counsel.text: It is the property of faith to silence our doubtings, to scatter our fears, to still the heart when the passions are up. Faith works the heart to a sweet serene composure; it is not having food and raiment, but having faith, which will make us content. Faith chides down passion; when reason begins to sink, let faith swim.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 14

counsel.text: So will be thy relief from Christ. It will come in its season, as the dew and rain upon the parched ground; for faithful is he who hath promised.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: God only is the fit object of trust. He hath all the properties of that which should be trusted on. A man can be in no condition wherein God is at a loss and cannot help him. If comforts be wanting, he can create comforts, not only out of nothing, but out of discomforts.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 16

counsel.text: After we have rolled ourselves upon God, we should immediately take that course he inclines our hearts unto, without further distracting fear. Otherwise it is a sign we 'commit not our way to him,' 1 Pet. 4. 19, when we do not quietly trust him, but remain still as thoughtful as if we did not trust him.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 17

counsel.text: It is no matter how heavy the burden is, if God gives a shoulder to bear it: all is in love; it is no matter how bitter the cup is, if God give courage to drink it off; it is no matter how hot the furnace is, if God gives power to walk in the midst of it: all is in love.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

counsel.text: Well! Christians, your shield of faith is safe, your portion is safe, your royal robe is safe, your kingdom is safe, your heaven is safe, your happiness and blessedness is safe; and therefore under all your afflictions and troubles, in patience possess your own souls.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

counsel.text: Certainly if he bids us be careful for none of these things, but only let our requests be made known to him, he intends not our loss by our ease, but thereby would have us understand and believe that he will take the care upon himself, and give us at last a full account of his love and faithfulness in the issue of his providence, how all was disposed for our best advantage.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Every day hath its portion, yea, proportion. Sufficient is the evil of the day; we need not borrow and take up sorrows upon use of the morrow, to make up our present load.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.opening: Almighty and faithful Father, you number the hairs of my head, feed the birds of the air, and clothe the grass of the field, and nothing comes to pass apart from your will; I bless you that I may come to you through Jesus Christ.
prayers.text: I confess that I have worried. I have carried tomorrow in my own arms as if you were not my Father. I have doubted your power, your wisdom, and your love. I have prayed little and fretted much, and I have let fear crowd out faith and service. Underneath my worry is a heart that wants to be in control, and does not trust you to be. My worry is unbelief, and it dishonors you. Forgive me, Lord. In the garden Christ entrusted himself to you, saying, Not my will, but yours, be done, and he now reigns over all things for his church. For his sake pardon me. Holy Spirit, put this anxious unbelief to death, and teach me to cast all my cares on you, because you care for me. Guard my heart and mind with your peace, which surpasses all understanding.
prayers.closing: I thank you that you will supply every need of mine according to your riches in glory in Christ Jesus. To our God and Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.

prayers.title: When worry rushes in
prayers.opening: O Lord, my shepherd, you know my going out and my coming in, and you hold my tomorrow in your hand.
prayers.text: Lord, my thoughts are racing ahead to what might happen. Stop me, and bring me back to today. You know what I need before I ask. I cast this care on you right now, and I name it before you. Help me not to be anxious about tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Give me grace to do the next duty in front of me and to leave the rest with you. Lord Jesus, you calmed the wind and the sea with a word; calm my heart.
prayers.closing: Blessed be your name, for you care for me. Amen.

prayers.title: When I am afraid
prayers.opening: My Father and my refuge, under the shadow of your wings I take shelter.
prayers.text: Father, I am afraid, and I thank you that I may tell you so. You are my refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. You have not given me a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control. Remind me that I am held in your hand, and that no one can snatch me from it. Whatever comes today will not come without your will, and you will turn it for my good. Let me trust you in the dark as in the light.
prayers.closing: Through Jesus Christ, who holds all things together, to whom be glory for ever. Amen.

prayers.title: Casting our care upon our Father
prayers.opening: Thou art the God that hast fed us all our life long unto this day, and redeemed us from all evil. It is of thy mercies that we are not consumed, even because thy compassions fail not, they are new every morning, great is thy faithfulness.
prayers.text: Father, we ask not for bread for a great while to come, but that we may have this day our daily bread; for we would learn, and the Lord teach us, not to take thought for the morrow, what we shall eat, or what we shall drink, or wherewithal we shall be clothed; but we cast the care upon thee, our heavenly Father, who knowest that we have need of all these things; who feedest the fowls of the air, though they sow not, neither do they reap, and wilt much more feed us, who are of more value than many sparrows.
prayers.closing: Do for us exceeding abundantly above what we are able to ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us: And supply all our needs according to thy riches in glory by Christ Jesus. To God, only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry
prayers.source: arranged from A Method for Prayer, chs. 1, 8 and 7

examinationQuestions: What were you anxious about today, and when the fear came, did you bring it to your Father or carry it alone?
Beneath the worry, what were you doubting about God: his power, his wisdom, or his love for you in Christ?
Which of God's promises did you forget today, and what would change if you believed it?
Are you trying to carry tomorrow's troubles with today's strength?
Has worry crowded out prayer, rest, or the Lord's Day, or kept you from serving others?
fleeActions: Tell God the worry out loud in one plain sentence, and leave it with him. Then turn to what you can do in the next hour.
Read Matthew 6:25-34 slowly, and ask your Father to help you trust him for today only.
Write down the thing you are afraid of, and beside it write one promise of God from his Word that answers it.
Ask a brother or sister in your church to pray for you today. Tell them plainly what you are afraid of.
Do the next ordinary duty in front of you, and do it as for the Lord. Leave tomorrow with him.
If this fear is heavy or keeps coming back, send your pastor a message today and ask to talk. Seeing a doctor as well is wise, not faithless.

afterFallReadings.text: Whether a Christian may not be sensible of his condition, and yet be contented? Yes; for else he is not a saint, but a stoic. Rachel did well to weep for her children, there was nature; but her fault was, she refused to be comforted, there was discontent.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 5

afterFallReadings.text: Consider his mercifulness, tenderness, and kindness, as he is our great High Priest at the right hand of God. Assuredly he pities thee in thy distress; saith he, "As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you," Isa. 66:13. He hath the tenderness of a mother to a sucking child.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
